
### theoretical model: alternating bit  {.smaller}


* let's say we can split up packets into individual bits
* fair sharing: <br> one bit from A, one bit from B, one bit from A, one bit from B, one bit from A, etc. 
<hr class="vspace" />
* preview:
* figure out what timing would look like if we could do this
* use this timing to decide what packets to send  

   * (the way we can actually send packets)

### using this order 


* computed the order packets ‘‘should’’ be received in
* goal: achieve same order but without bit-by-bit
* … by sending packets in desired receive order

### rounds versus steps {.smaller}


* alternating bit: 
   * several rounds where we transmit 1 bit from each pending flow
   * number of steps per round varies depending on number of active flows
* can think of round number as a weird notion of time 
   * time "slows down" when there are more pending flows
   * less precise than number of steps, but...
   * arbitrarily chose which flow went first/last in round
* easier to compute _number of rounds_ than _number of steps_
